Write _n for the free group on n generators and _infty for the free group on countably infinitely many generators. The free group factors arose in Murray and von Neumann's foundational work (murray_vonneumann1943). Their nonhyperfiniteness distinguished them from the hyperfinite factor, but did not distinguish their ranks; see the historical account in (radulescu1992, p. 518). The question whether L( _m) and L( _n) are isomorphic for distinct m,n 2 became a central problem in the classification of finite factors. Dykema's introduction (dykema1994, p. 123) records the early history and credits Kadison with raising the rank-isomorphism question.

Free probability supplied a way to study these factors through their generating distributions. Voiculescu developed the reduced-free-product framework (voiculescu1985) and its semicircular and circular models (voiculescu1990). His compression results showed that the fundamental group of L( _infty) contains every positive rational, and R adulescu extended this to every positive real number (radulescu1992). Dykema and R adulescu independently constructed the interpolated factors L( _r) for real r>1 and established their amplification calculus (dykema1994,radulescu1994). These results relate changes of rank to normalized corners. They also give a dichotomy: the interpolated free group factors are either all isomorphic or pairwise nonisomorphic. The version including the infinite parameter is due to R adulescu (radulescu1994, Corollary 4.7); see also the precise restatement in (goldbring_pi2025, Theorem 1.1).

The amplification calculus thus links rank to corner size, while the dichotomy reduces the classification to two alternatives. To choose the isomorphic alternative, it suffices to construct an isomorphism between two distinct finite ranks. Our constructive result is the following rank comparison.
